items.independence_limits: Fresh-context reviewer; cold pass written (notes/review-17-cold-pass.md) before opening the packet. Did not read earlier reviews, provenance/ (except writing the inventory) or git history; used the pre-edit copy in paper/downloaded/ only to verify the post-writer Appendix A edit. Numbers were spot-checked (45 entries in editorial-review-17.json), not exhaustively; R replay not rerun; live master URLs not fetched (pre-merge gate only). Human scientific review is still needed.

findings.finding: Opens 'We did not replicate the three simulation headlines of Chen (2021), who reported biased direct-effect estimates, percentile bootstrap intervals that cover the true value far too rarely, and power for the mediated interaction (MINT) near zero: 85.42% ... against 0.00% ...; 43.62 ... against 0.04; ... 0.013 (raw 0.063) ... against 0.802 (raw 0.852).' Verdict, cited source, original findings and all paired headline numbers in one sentence; the headline missed and the sentence says so.

H4 'holds only in part' with 86.3%/89.2%; limit sentence on restricted-use Head Start data and unseeded bootstrap follows; tolerances and 'point-estimate comparisons, not equivalence' closes. No reversal exists and none is invented.

Polish: 'the three simulation headlines' reads as if there were only three; H4 is also a simulation headline (Section 1 calls it 'Her fourth headline'). Not misleading in substance because H4 is reported in the next sentence and in Table 1 row E5; suggest 'three of her four simulation headlines'.

Opens 'We did not replicate the simulation headlines of Chen (2021)' with 85.42% vs 0.00%, 24.10-83.99% vs 94.6-95.6% coverage, 0.063 vs 0.852 (0.013 vs 0.802 above .05); then MC standard errors (.007; .002), H4 'holds for most but not all cells', the limit (Head Start, unseeded bootstrap) and 'No estimate reverses its sign.'
Tolerances restated (half a unit of her last decimal; figure-reading error) and labelled as point-estimate comparisons, not equivalence tests.

Polish: 'The disagreements therefore arise in steps she did not print' is slightly stronger than Section 6.1, which attributes much of the disagreement to the data behind her published runs (a run differing from the printed code); consider 'in steps or runs she did not print'.

Should-fix (non-failing): '(1,270 datasets, of which the 635 kept by the replay were compared)' is unexplained and attributes the 635 to 'the replay'. In r-reproduction/chen_exact.R the literal check deliberately keeps every other dataset of block 0 to test that skipping preserves data and RNG state; the full 1,000-replication replay keeps all 1,280,000. Table 2 (p. 6) says identity was 'verified on the first simulation block (1,270 datasets)'. Neither statement is false (RNG state over all 1,270; values over 635), but a reader can wrongly infer the replay keeps half the datasets. Fix: 'the check rebuilt every other dataset (635) and skipped the rest; the 635 are identical and the random-number state after all 1,270 is identical', and align Table 2.
Defines MINT, RDD, HSIS, PNDE/TNDE on first use; no references to earlier drafts, reviewers or internal roles; every evidence pointer is an exact filename.

Reproduction recipe separated from scientific prose; names README section 'Reproduce'; says outputs not committed and source PDF must be downloaded. Only 'master' is named; no commit hash or working branch anywhere (commit_refs.py accepted).

All seven packet limitations present and in order (limitations_map verified). Item 1 is hedged more than the packet ('evidently ... an inference from her figures'), which is appropriate, not an understatement.
Claim-specific limits preserved: H3 read from image at cutoffs 2-3 with 0.0091 reading error; H4 tentative vs literal; S1 zero-estimate pattern partial; S5 divisor intent unknown.

Post-hoc choice of the E4 cell is disclosed ('chosen after the full results were available') and Section 7.5 (p. 17) says the 0.0091 tolerance was 'not set in the plan'. Polish: page 1 does not mention the post-hoc cell choice; one clause in the Table 1 caption would close this.

Separates Chen's contribution (model, design, definitions, printed numbers) from ours (Python re-implementation, exact R replay, digitizing, statement checks, Head Start arithmetic, disagreement tests) and labels each number's origin.

Engine departure (Python first used without asking the owner, then agreed; full R bootstrap declined) is disclosed and justified, matching simulation/fallback.json and the Appendix B ledger. It is process narration, but it affects interpretation (bootstrap results agree only in distribution), so it belongs.
Blocked Head Start parts called 'blocked: not established, and not a failure to replicate'; S8 'not established, and nothing blocks it'. Nothing blocked is called a nonreplication.

Chen (2021) identity verified on source/chen2021.pdf (SHA-256 9206b3d8...e557, 203 pages) title page: Donna Chen, 'Statistical Mediation Analysis in Regression Discontinuity Design for Causal Inference', University of Nebraska, December 2021, advisers Bovaird and Wheeler; Digital Commons cehsdiss/403 identifier matches packet replicated_work.

Source passages located: negative direct-effect bias (PDF p. 161/printed 147, 'When bias was present, the measure of bias was a negative value'); true value 'systematically fell above the CIs' (PDF p. 164/printed 150); 'All power for MINT is near zero' (PDF p. 135/printed 121); 'Tentatively, a minimum sample size of 5000 ...' (PDF p. 164); opposite significance conclusions (abstract PDF p. 3; PDF p. 157/printed 143).
'her abstract and Chapter 5 (printed p. 143) say that Type I error and power for all five effects were within or reached the robustness criteria' verified at PDF pp. 3 and 157.

E1 0.005 and E2 0.005 (mean of values each printed to 2 decimals), E3 0.01 (difference of two such means), E4 0.0091 = mean of reading errors 0.0052 and 0.0131 = 0.00915 rounded down, measurement kind, not called prespecified. Derivations verified.

findings.finding: E1 smaller / zero vs nonzero (ours 0.00 within 0.005 of zero); E2 smaller / same (0.0358 > 0.005); E3 smaller / same; E4 larger / same (her 0.0127 exceeds 0.0091, so not zero by the rule); E5 not established x2. All labels follow the first-page contract.

'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.' present; estimands, units, positive meaning stated; Monte Carlo error pointed to Section 1 (.007 per cell, E2/E3 means 0.005-0.019 from results/mc_se_headline.json, E4 about .002); 'Chen reports none'.

Published 'within [-.10, .10] in only 12.50-18.75% of conditions, with negative bias' matches dissertation Table 4.8 PNDE/TNDE rows (12.50, 12.50, 18.75) and printed p. 147. Ours 'within [-.05, .05] in 100% of conditions; largest |bias| 0.016' matches results/table48_ours.csv (max 0.0155 for direct effects; overall max 0.01551 in summary.json).

Published 'Coverage 24.10-83.99%; true value usually above the CI' matches Table 4.9 (min TNDE1 24.10, max PNIE3 83.99; above > below in every row). Ours 'Coverage 94.6-95.6%; misses on both sides at similar rates' matches table49_ours.csv (94.59-95.63; below 1.84-2.71, above 2.52-2.90).

Published 'MINT power near zero ...; never reaches .80 (Figure 4.28: 0.057-0.068 in this cell)' matches printed p. 121 and digitized readings 0.0571/0.0683 (status read). Ours '0.852 at cutoffs 2-3 (0.836 over all cutoffs); at least .97 for ah >= .13 from n = 1,000' matches digitized_rates.csv our_value and summary.json (0.8361; min 0.9735).

Published quotes the tentative recommendation (PDF p. 164). Ours '86.3% ... 89.2% ..., similar at each cutoff; both-zero products stay conservative' matches statement_checks.csv n = 5000 rows (86.3%; 89.2%; cutoffs 85.7-87.0 / 88.3-89.9) and disagreement_tests.json n5000.both_paths_zero.
